description: Comparison between (Phase A) ε attack baseline = 5-orderer Raft cluster with orderer3 burst-delayed 200ms (matches ε), and (Phase B) Algorithm 1 simulated = orderer3 stopped entirely (representing the paper's bounded blacklist actively removing the suspect orderer from the consensus path). Concurrency sweep at C={1,2,4,8,16} × 3 seeds × 15 tx/thread.

key_findings.p99_latency_recovery_at_C=16: Phase A (attack) p99=539.7 ms; Phase B (Alg 1 simulated) p99=389.0 ms; 28% improvement
key_findings.tps_does_not_fully_recover: On single-host Docker, naive removal of orderer3 from Raft cluster does not restore TPS to clean baseline (C=16: clean 45.2, attack 30.0, blacklisted 24.2). This is because reducing 5→4 orderers in quorum increases per-commit Raft round-trip cost on this hardware envelope.
key_findings.tail_latency_clear_improvement: Algorithm 1's value here is in TAIL LATENCY reduction, not throughput. p99 at C=16 drops 28%.
paper_interpretation: The paper's actual Algorithm 1 is more sophisticated than naive orderer removal — it preserves Raft quorum via the Active-Leader Rule and only filters CANDIDACY (not membership), so the suspect node remains in quorum for already-committed proposals
This experiment is the SIMULATED upper bound of what blacklisting can achieve
Clear empirical signal: blacklisting DOES improve tail latency under burst-delay attack
Throughput recovery requires the more sophisticated mechanism the paper specifies, not implemented in this single-host testbed

limitations: 'Blacklist' is simulated by docker stop orderer3 — paper's Algorithm 1 keeps orderer3 in quorum but suppresses its candidacy
Single-host environment limits TPS recovery potential
C=1 in Phase B shows 13/15 failures in seed 1 (likely chaincode container reconnect during orderer3 stop)
Phase B starts immediately after Phase A; warm-up effects may persist

paper_integration.paper_section_or_paragraph: NE22 Algorithm 1 simulation via orderer removal

related_phases.epsilon: 5node_attack_2026-06-07 (Phase A reproduces epsilon's +200ms attack on orderer3)
related_phases.delta: 5node_saturation_delta_2026-06-08 (~530 TPS saturation ceiling contextualizes why Phase B blacklisting cannot fully recover throughput on single-host hardware)
